headline: Today complete: cycling exceeded the morning easy-run prescription
summary: The early-morning brief recommended 35–45 minutes of easy running. Garmin later recorded a 69m 31s, 30.52 km cycling activity with training load 114, aerobic effect 3.2, and anaerobic effect 1.4. This was a meaningful training session rather than the planned easy run; do no further training today.

yesterday.title: Morning easy-run prescription versus a cycling session
yesterday.summary: The early-morning report prescribed 35–45 minutes of easy conversational running, without speedwork. Garmin later recorded one cycling activity and no run on 13 September.
yesterday.prescribed: 35–45 minutes easy and conversational running, with no intervals, hills, tempo running, or strides. The approved lower-load alternative was 20–30 minutes walking or rest.
yesterday.completed: One cycling activity: 30.52 km in 1h 09m 31s, average HR 144, maximum HR 167, training load 114, aerobic effect 3.2, anaerobic effect 1.4, and 306 m elevation gain.
yesterday.adherence_assessment: The completed cycling session was not the prescribed easy run or an approved lower-load alternative. Its measured duration and training load were greater than the planned 35–45 minute easy session.
adherence_evidence: Garmin lists one cycling activity with a 13 September Sydney start time and no run.
The ride lasted 1h 09m 31s and carried training load 114.
Garmin recorded aerobic effect 3.2 and anaerobic effect 1.4.
adherence_caveats: Garmin cannot verify perceived effort, pain, illness, terrain intent, or why the activity was completed.
Heart-rate data may differ across devices; no alternate-sensor data was used.

environment.observed_temperature_range: 19–28°C recorded by the Garmin device during the ride.
environment.humidity_dew_point_context: A reliable route-time Sydney humidity and dew-point estimate was not available, so none was used.
environment.heat_impact_interpretation: The warmer device readings could contribute to heart rate or pace. That is coaching context, not proof of heat strain and not the reason for the adherence verdict.
environment.limitations: Garmin temperature is a device measurement and may be affected by body heat and local exposure; it is not an official city observation.

recommendation.title: No further training today
details: The morning recommendation was 35–45 minutes of easy running. Garmin instead records a 69-minute cycling session with training load 114.
Do no further running, riding, intervals, hills, tempo work, or make-up distance today.
Optional only: 10–20 minutes of easy walking or gentle mobility if it feels restorative.
recommendation.alternative: Complete rest is the safe lower-load alternative.
recommendation.reduce_or_stop: Stop optional activity for pain, illness, dizziness, altered gait, unusual fatigue, chest symptoms, or other concerning symptoms. Symptoms and medical advice override Garmin scores.

signals.interpretation: These were supportive of exercise but do not require additional work after the completed ride.

signals.interpretation: Short sleep remains a reason to keep the rest of the day recovery-focused.

caveats: Garmin sleep, heart-rate, HRV, stress, Body Battery, readiness, and load measures are wearable-derived; use trends alongside how you feel.
Today's stress and Body Battery values are incomplete morning measures.
Sleeping-heart-rate baselines exclude the current night and use the prior seven and fourteen valid nights.
Garmin device temperature and city-level weather estimates are distinct from route-level conditions.

run_assessments.assessment: The cycling session did not follow the morning prescription of 35–45 minutes easy running or its lower-load alternatives. Garmin recorded 1h 09m 31s, 30.52 km, training load 114, aerobic effect 3.2 and anaerobic effect 1.4, so it was a larger measured training stimulus than the prescribed easy session. The 19–28°C device temperature is contextual only.
